description: Species code matching fresh's parameters_habitat_thresholds.csv (BT, CH, CO, ST, WCT, SK, KO, PK, CM, RB, CT, DV, GR). Row key.
Does the species spawn in lakes? When yes, lnk_rules_build emits a `waterbody_type: L` rule under spawn:.
Does the species spawn in streams? When yes, lnk_rules_build emits the stream-edge rule (edge_types_explicit: [1000, 1100, 2000, 2300]) plus the river polygon rule (waterbody_type: R) under spawn:.

Should the spawn-stream rule fire on segments INSIDE a waterbody polygon (waterbody_key non-null)? `no` emits `in_waterbody: false` so the stream rule matches only outside-polygon segments - strict partition that pairs with the polygon rules. `yes` (or absent) omits the field; rule matches both inside and outside polygons.

Does the species rear in lakes? When yes (and not rear_lake_only / rear_no_fw), lnk_rules_build emits a `waterbody_type: L` rule admitting lines inside lake and reservoir polygons - edge_types_explicit: [1000, 1100, 1200, 1250, 1300, 1350, 1400, 1450, 1475], since lakes carry construction lines rather than mainlines and reservoirs on rivers also hold double-line river flow lines 1250 / 1350 (#310) - with thresholds: false (no channel-width or discharge test) + lake_ha_min from rear_lake_ha_min or fresh thresholds. The 1450 connectors stay in `rearing` (they join inlet rearing to the lake for cluster_rearing) and the compare rollups report them as rearing_lake_connection km, outside rearing km (#317).
emits: waterbody_type: L + lake-centreline edge filter + thresholds: false (rear, additive branch)

description: Override: this species ONLY rears in lakes. When yes, lnk_rules_build emits a single `waterbody_type: L` rule under rear:, no edge filter, no other rules. Used by SK, KO. lake_ha_min still honoured.

When yes, emits `area_only: true` on the L polygon rule. fresh derives the lake_rearing bucket flag but excludes the rule from the main rear predicate. Linear `rearing_km` excludes polygon segments; `lake_rearing_ha` still rolls up. Only honoured in the additive rear branch - rear_lake_only ignores this column (the L rule there IS the rear classification).
Override: species has no freshwater rearing (CM, PK). When yes, all rear rules are dropped. Higher precedence than rear_lake / rear_stream / etc.
Does the species rear in streams? When yes (and not rear_lake_only / rear_no_fw), lnk_rules_build emits the stream-edge rule + the river polygon rule under rear:.

Should the rear-stream rule fire on segments INSIDE a waterbody polygon? Same shape as spawn_stream_in_waterbody. `no` emits `in_waterbody: false` (strict partition matching bcfishpass's per-species access SQL). `yes` (or absent) is permissive - counts polygon-mainlines as rearing.

Does the species rear in wetland-flow segments? When yes, lnk_rules_build emits the 1050/1150 stream-flow carve-out (edge_types_explicit: [1050, 1150], thresholds: false) under rear:. With a rear_wetland_ha_min and the W polygon rule emitted, the carve-out also carries waterbody_type: W + wetland_ha_min and follows the polygon rule (#311). The W polygon rule is gated separately by rear_wetland_polygon.

Should lnk_rules_build emit the `waterbody_type: W` polygon rule (drives wetland_rearing flag, populating wetland_rearing_ha rollup)? When yes (requires rear_wetland=yes), emits the W rule with edge_types_explicit: [1000, 1100] mainlines filter. When no (or absent), only the carve-out emits, unfloored, so the species has no W rule and no wetland_rearing bucket.
When yes, emits `area_only: true` on the W polygon rule. Same shape as rear_lake_area_only.

Override: drop the edge_types filter on the rear-stream rule (matches every accessible segment regardless of edge_type). Used by BT in bcfishpass bundle to match bcfishpass's BT rear access logic. Higher precedence than rear_stream's normal emission.

Should the river polygon rule (`waterbody_type: R`) skip the cw_min check? When yes, emits `channel_width: [0, 9999]` on the river rule - biology of large rivers spawning/rearing fish regardless of FWA cw measurement. Spawn-side bypass; complements the rearing stream_order bypass (rear_stream_order_bypass).

Gate for the rearing stream-order bypass. When yes, lnk_rules_build emits a `channel_width_min_bypass:` block on the rear stream-edge rule and lnk_pipeline_classify calls fresh::frs_order_child post-classify per species. Captures the biology of small streams plugging into large rivers: fish use these reaches for rearing despite low/missing FWA channel-width estimates. The bypass parameters (parent, child range, distance) are configured via the four `rear_stream_order_*` columns below. When no, the YAML block is dropped and the post-classify call is skipped entirely.

Minimum stream order at the trib BLK's mouth confluence (i.e. the order of the receiving stream). Maps to fresh::frs_order_child(parent_order_min). Default 5 matches bcfishpass's hardcoded predicate. Only honoured when rear_stream_order_bypass=yes.

Lower bound on the bypass-eligible segment's own stream_order. Maps to fresh::frs_order_child(child_order_min). Default 1. Combined with rear_stream_order_child_max defines a range of segment orders to credit. Only honoured when rear_stream_order_bypass=yes.

Upper bound on the bypass-eligible segment's own stream_order. Maps to fresh::frs_order_child(child_order_max). Default 1 (single-order tribs only — bcfp parity). Set higher to widen — e.g. 5 captures order-1..5 single-order tribs feeding order-5+ stems. Only honoured when rear_stream_order_bypass=yes.

Cap (metres) on the bypass-eligible segment's downstream_route_measure — credits only the lower N m of each direct-trib BLK from its mouth confluence. Maps to fresh::frs_order_child(distance_max). Empty = no cap (whole BLK up to gradient/access limits). Only honoured when rear_stream_order_bypass=yes.

Habitat type that spawn rules' segments must be connected to (e.g. "rearing" for SK / KO - spawning happens within reach of rearing lakes). When set, every emitted spawn rule carries `requires_connected: <value>`.
Max network distance (metres) between a spawn segment and the connected target. When set with spawn_requires_connected, every spawn rule carries `connected_distance_max: <value>`.
Direction to walk from spawn segment when looking for the connected target. Drives the spawn_connected: block in rules.yaml.
Bridge gradient cap when tracing toward the connected target. Drives spawn_connected.gradient_max.
Channel width minimum on the trace to the connected target. Drives spawn_connected.channel_width_min.
Semicolon-separated list of edge_type integers permitted on the trace toward the connected target. Drives spawn_connected.edge_types.

fresh#191 knob on .frs_connected_waterbody Phase 2 (upstream spawn). When yes (bcfp parity), the SK upstream-spawn cluster + lake-adjacency gate fires (spawning credited only for clusters within 2 m of a qualifying rearing lake polygon). When no, the cluster gate is dropped — every spawn-eligible segment upstream of and accessible from a qualifying rearing waterbody is credited. Empty = inherits fresh's default (TRUE).

RETIRED (#310). Stamped requires_connected on every rear rule, which fresh >= 0.37.0 refuses on all but the first rear L / W rule. Kept as a column so older bundles build: lnk_rules_build ignores it when empty and stops when it carries a value. Use rear_lake_connected_distance_max / rear_wetland_connected_distance_max.
RETIRED (#310); see rear_requires_connected. Ignored when empty, stops the build when set.
Per-species override for the L polygon rule's lake_ha_min. When set, wins over fresh's parameters_habitat_thresholds.csv value. Honoured in both rear_lake_only and additive rear branches.

Per-species minimum wetland area (ha) for both wetland rear rules (the stream rule still admits mainlines in smaller wetlands). It sets wetland_ha_min on the W polygon rule and also turns the 1050/1150 carve-out into a W rule carrying the same floor, emitted after the polygon rule so the polygon rule stays fresh's first W rule (#311). From fresh 0.38.0 the floor gates `rearing` as well as `wetland_rearing` (fresh#237). Blank means no floor; with no floor, or with rear_wetland_polygon = no, the carve-out stays unfloored. fresh has no wetland threshold column, so this is the only source.
emits: wetland_ha_min on the W polygon rule; waterbody_type: W + wetland_ha_min on the 1050/1150 carve-out

description: Metres. When set, the species' first rear `waterbody_type: L` rule carries requires_connected: spawning + connected_distance_max, so fresh keeps a lake in the lake_rearing bucket only where same-species spawning lies on it, or within this distance downstream of it, or within this distance upstream traced down mainstem lines (fresh#240). The bucket reads fwa_lakes_poly only (fresh v0.39.0), so a reservoir is never lake_rearing and the distance never applies to one. Blank = every lake passing the area test. Must be > 0. Refused for a species with spawn_requires_connected = rearing (SK, KO: circular). Only the bucket is filtered; lake line km in `rearing` follow the rearing cluster pass.
emits: requires_connected: spawning + connected_distance_max on the first rear L rule

description: Metres. Same as rear_lake_connected_distance_max for the first rear `waterbody_type: W` rule (the polygon rule, not the floored 1050/1150 rule after it) and the wetland_rearing bucket.
emits: requires_connected: spawning + connected_distance_max on the first rear W rule

description: Free-form notes per species - biology references, citations, NGE-vs-bcfishpass deltas, TODO lifelines. Not consumed by lnk_rules_build.
